A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central claims and original experiments. The text, equations, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including the new Appendix E in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model experiments on CIFAR-10, CelebA, text8, LAION-10k and Random Hierarchy Model data, including results in Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds numerical score-learning experiments on Gaussian data in Appendix E, Figures 14–16.

M1.justification: The early-stopping proposal and existing diffusion-model training and sampling procedures are unchanged. Appendix E introduces analytical and experimental probes of score learning, rather than a revised generative method.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds Gaussian-distributed vectors in 64 dimensions for empirical-score fitting at fixed diffusion noise. This is a limited synthetic extension; the existing image, language and hierarchical-grammar coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. The new NTK and feature-learning initializations are controlled conditions in the scaling analysis; the cited random-feature results are theoretical comparisons, not newly evaluated benchmark baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a distinct controlled evaluation protocol: fixed-noise score fitting with a one-hidden-layer network, NTK versus mean-field initialization, noise and dataset-size sweeps, and full-batch versus stochastic gradient descent. Figures 14–16 cover P=128–2048 and batch sizes B=8–128. Existing diffusion-experiment settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 14–16 add substantial diagnostic analyses testing the predicted noise and dataset-size scaling, its persistence under feature learning, and sensitivity to batch size. These directly investigate the mechanism and robustness of the central memorization-time law; v1 lacks these analyses.

E5.justification: Existing error-bar displays and statistical reporting are retained. Appendix E adds no reported seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 14–16 newly report memorization times consistent with linear dependence on dataset size, inverse dependence on noise standard deviation under both initializations, and approximate batch-size independence. These are new findings in the Gaussian setting. Existing results and Figures 1–13 remain unchanged, including CIFAR-10 FID 5.4 with 0% copies.

T1.justification: New Appendix E develops a kernel-operator scaling argument using separated Gaussian components, localized score-mode ansatz functions and Rayleigh quotients, obtaining tau_mem proportional to P/sigma^nu. It distinguishes ReLU NTK and random-feature exponents. Section 2 also corrects the empirical distribution by inserting the missing 1/P normalization.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a theoretical contribution: explaining dataset-size scaling for kernel methods at fixed, low diffusion noise. The abstract and central claims about generalization before memorization, early stopping and the hierarchical phase diagram retain their previous scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds a spectral interpretation of memorization time, interprets agreement under feature learning as extending beyond fixed kernels, and links batch-size independence to optimization steps rather than repeated exposures. Section 5 distinguishes diffusion memorization from noisy supervised regression. The conclusion removes v1's explicit limitation concerning explanation of the law for deep, time-dependent diffusion architectures.

D1.justification: Appendix E documents the added experiment's ReLU activation, single hidden layer, width 8192, data dimension, initialization regimes and optimization conditions. Existing Appendix A hyperparameters, hardware information and code-access links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through explicit comparison with Bonnaire et al.'s random-feature analysis, earlier Gaussian-approximation learning, and supervised double descent and benign overfitting. It adds relevant kernel and mean-field references while retaining the earlier cited works.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 1.1 to Section 5, the conclusion is renumbered, and Section 3.3 gains a theoretical-support discussion. Local wording and explanatory edits accompany these changes, but most existing prose and the main experimental narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 14–16 with paired panels, rescaled-axis plots, insets and legends for the new experiments. Existing Figures 1–13 retain their graphical content, with limited caption edits and changes to placement and surrounding text flow.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly lacked an explanation for its central memorization-time scaling law. v2 substantially strengthens that argument through a kernel scaling derivation and controlled tests of noise, dataset size, initialization and batch size in Appendix E. Removing the explicit deep-architecture limitation weakens qualification, since the new theory addresses a restricted setting. Nevertheless, its assumptions remain stated, and the added explanatory and diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
